plan: Name the capability each decision belongs to, so the fold knows where it goes

specs-living-model: A source file reports the living specs that claim it, in the editor's own process
Requirement slicing lives beside the requirement-id parser and counts the same headings

ai-providers-config: A stale or unknown provider setting never breaks activation
ai-providers-dispatch: Every assistant is reached through one provider contract
Terminal CLIs share one dispatch lifecycle

Dispatch targets are probed at dispatch time, not assumed

ai-providers-prompt: Bookkeeping instructions travel separately from the user-facing command

concerns.note: Two lifecycle capture calls failed early in this run: a shell function wrapping write-context.py did not resolve, so the calls exited without recording. Both were immediately re-run successfully. History is append-only, so the failed pair cannot be removed.

The doctor reports real drift on nine capabilities (specs-state-record, the seven viewer-ui-* files, ai-providers-*) against baseline 9b00a320. None of it was caused by this run; it predates the branch and belongs to the living-specs fold backlog, not to this spec.

The stale-extension warning is raised on the next start rather than mid-session. When a check learns a newer published version during a session that had already decided not to warn, nothing re-syncs the surfaces. This is a deliberate scope call recorded in the spec assumptions.
